text:
Mia (Marketing): Quick thread to finalize the benchmark hero and two visual treatments. Need headline A/B, short supporting blurbs for PLG vs Enterprise, and final chart annotations. Goal: make latency vs cost story tangible and actionable for engineers + reassuring for enterprise buyers.

Diego (Content): For headline ideas: 1) 'Predictable latency. Predictable cost.' 2) 'Faster responses, clearer dollars.' 3) 'Serve reliably. Pay sensibly.' I'd favor 1 for clarity. Also propose two email subject lines: (A) 'See how we trade latency for dollars' (B) 'Benchmark: speed, cost, and how to control both'.

Sam (Data): I'm preparing the canonical dataset. Quick suggestion on visuals: Treatment A = scatter (median ms x-axis, cost per 1k y-axis) with small variant markers (cache, quant). Treatment B = stacked CDFs showing 50/95/99 bands for representative workloads with shaded SLA thresholds.

Lina (Design): I'll mock both. Visual rules: use single strong accent for Redwood points, grey for competitor/benchmark points; small annotation badges for 'cache on' and 'quantized'. For the scatter, we'll show arrows with short phrases like 'batching -> lower cost' and 'cache -> lower latency'. For the CDF, annotate 95/99 lines with 'SLA risk zone' (light red).

Noah (Growth): A/B test plan: run hero headline A vs B on site. Drive traffic from newsletter and paid. Track on-page CTA CTR, time to first token (simulated via demo), and inbound form conversion. Include UTM params: utm_campaign=bench_launch_170460. Also include hidden field that tags whether viewer saw visual A or B.

Raj (Product): Add product note copy: 'Routing and fallback policies keep applications online: when Dedicated is constrained, we route to compatible quantized variants with marginal latency increase and lower cost.' Keep it short for the subhead.

Sam (Data): CSV snippet for Lina to mock with. Columns: workload,variant,median_ms,p95_ms,cost_per_1k_usd,notes

Sam (Data): ```
workload,variant,median_ms,p95_ms,cost_per_1k_usd,notes
chat,redwood-quant,40,170,0.011,baseline
chat,redwood-quant+cache,26,115,0.007,prefix cache on
summarize,open-gt3,130,620,0.048,high-quality long seqs
embed,embed-lite,16,38,0.005,short tokens
```

Lina (Design): Got it. I'll produce two PNGs and an interactive mock (hover tooltips) for web. Will include a compact footnote area: measurement conditions (GPU type, median over N=300 requests, seq len distribution).

Diego (Content): For captions under the chart: PLG caption (concise): 'Engineers: pick the right control — batching, cache, quantization — to optimize cost/latency for your workload.' Enterprise caption: 'Enterprises: predictable 95/99 latency SLAs with Dedicated + automated fallbacks to maintain availability.' Keep each ~15 words.

Noah (Growth): Also propose a short webinar CTA line to reuse in email and hero: 'Join a 30-min demo: how we shave tail latency and unit cost.' Link to registration with utm. We'll route registrants into SDR queue tagged 'bench_launch_170460'.

Mia (Marketing): Nice. Action items: Sam -> upload full CSV + a 3-sentence methods blurb; Lina -> scatter + CDF PNGs + interactive mock; Diego -> finalize two headline variants + email subject lines; Raj -> 1-sentence product fallback blurb; Noah -> tracking/UTM + routing for registrants. I'll assemble the landing page copy and the email copy tonight and share for review tomorrow AM.

Sam (Data): Dropping measurement blurb: 'Measurements collected on A100-equivalent GPUs, tokenization=BPE, median and p95 computed over randomized samples of production-like request traces. Cost estimates reflect model execution + infra overhead.' I'll add full dataset to the Drive folder in 30m.

AssetBot: Uploaded assets to https://drive.redwood.dev/bench/1704606789/ (scatter_v2.png, cdf_v2.png, interactive_mock.html).

Lina (Design): Mock uploads complete. Ping me for tweaks on callouts.

Diego (Content): I'm drafting the landing headline A/B and 2 short descriptions; will post copies here for quick sign-off.

Mia (Marketing): Great work team. We'll review the assembled landing + email tomorrow. This thread is canonical for benchmark visuals and headline A/B. :rocket:
